judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Link 1 of the tile row (to the ESOU 'Fale com a Ouvidoria' form). The four image links in the first h2 (Fale com a Ouvidoria -> ESOU form at www3, Perguntas mais frequentes -> FAQ page, Estatisticas -> statistics page, Balcao virtual -> Azure video-counter app) all carry aria-label="Link sem descricao", which overrides the descriptive alt of their images: Chromium's tree in the snapshot gives each link the name "Link sem descricao" (nameFrom aria-label) and the h2 itself reads "Link sem descricao" four times. No title or aria-describedby; they share the same h2 block, so their context is identical. I opened the four destinations on the live page: four different, non-equivalent pages. The icon tiles visibly tell them apart. By R1 the set fails, and the name itself ("link without description") does not describe any purpose either; 2.5.3 also fails (visible tile text not in the name). Live HTML still has the same four aria-labels (two hrefs are now absolute portaltj URLs, same pages), so the capture matches. The claim names this failure: true_positive.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Case-number textbox #parte1ProcCNJ in the header search. Its label <label for> "Num. unica" has class d-none (display:none, confirmed in the live HTML); it also has a title and a placeholder. Chromium's own tree in the snapshot gives it name "" with a labelledby relation to that hidden label and no description: Blink takes the hidden label as the name source, gets empty text and does not fall back to the title or placeholder. So in Chrome/Edge, what most users run, the field has no accessible name, a 4.1.2 failure (HTML-AAM would fall back to the title, which is why code-only review or axe may pass it). The claim states exactly this; 'announces only textbox' is close (NVDA may still voice the placeholder). Live markup unchanged.
